findings.title: No explicit success criteria
findings.problem: The system prompt states the role and scope but never defines what a successful recommendation or comparison looks like, so success is only implied by the rules.
findings.fix: Add a short 'Success' section to system_prompt.md stating what a good answer contains (top pick, caveats for missed constraints, sources cited) and what counts as abstaining correctly.

findings.title: No human escalation or oversight path
findings.problem: Nothing in the context provides a human review or escalation route for flagged, disputed or unresolved cases, which the Limited-risk transparency and evaluation obligations make relevant; this belongs in system_prompt.md.
findings.fix: Add an escalation rule to system_prompt.md that routes flagged results, repeated safety refusals and shopper complaints to a named human contact or logged review queue.

findings.title: No ranking or commercial-influence transparency rule
findings.problem: The context never tells the agent how products are ordered or whether sponsored or commercial placement can influence the table, which the recommendation use case requires to be disclosed; this belongs in system_prompt.md.
findings.fix: Add a rule to system_prompt.md stating the ranking basis (evidence fit, constraints, price) and that no paid or sponsored placement affects ordering, and have the table label say so.

findings.title: Reply-cap rule conflicts with multi-part replies
findings.problem: The rule caps non-grounded replies at three fixed sentences, yet the input screen also answers the rest of the message after a declined sentence, so a greeting plus declines plus a product answer has no defined precedence for the cap.
findings.proof: Every reply that is not grounded in tool results (a greeting, a statement about the assistant, a refusal) is assembled from the fixed sentences below, at most three.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to system_prompt.md defining which fixed sentences survive when the cap is exceeded (for example, declines first, then the product request).

findings.title: Redundant catalog category list in tool schema
findings.problem: The rag.search description repeats a full category list that the catalog file already gives, and the list is only a pointer to a resource the agent may not load.
findings.proof: Largest categories: toys & games, hobbies, home & kitchen, games & accessories, clothing, shoes & jewelry, costumes & accessories (all of them: resource catalog://categories).
findings.fix: Replace the list in the rag.search description with a one-line pointer to catalog://categories and keep the full list only in one file.

findings.title: Citation timestamp rule missing from system prompt
findings.problem: The system prompt tells the agent to cite live results but omits the retrieval-time requirement, which exists only in the knowledge file, so the Answerer may cite live prices without their age.
findings.proof: A live result is cited by its URL and the store or site name, with the time it was retrieved.
findings.fix: Add to system_prompt.md's Claims section that every live price or availability is cited with its URL, store and retrieved_at time.

findings.title: Untrusted-content stripping covers only web results
findings.problem: The stripping rule applies to web results only, and nothing in the context says catalog listings returned by rag.search, which carry titles and descriptions, are sanitized or fenced in the same way; this rule belongs in system_prompt.md.
findings.fix: Extend the untrusted-content rule in system_prompt.md to all tool results, including rag.search listings, and state that they are fenced as data in every prompt.

findings.title: Price-snapshot rule repeated across files
findings.problem: The January 2020 catalog price rule appears in both the system prompt and the knowledge file, duplicating context the model reads on every turn.
findings.proof: Prices are in US dollars and come from a January 2020 snapshot (median $16.99).
findings.fix: Keep the price-snapshot rule once in system_prompt.md Claims and drop the copy in catalog_and_sources.md, keeping only the median figure if it is needed.

findings.title: Escalation sentence duplicated in scope file
findings.problem: The hand-over rule for purchases, returns and complaints is restated in scope_and_policy.md after appearing in system_prompt.md, and the Safety policy and Router sections also restate the same declined categories.
findings.proof: What the assistant cannot do it hands over: purchases, returns and complaints to the store named with each product;
findings.fix: Keep one authoritative copy of the hand-over and declined-category lists and have the Router and scope file reference it rather than restate it.
